

```{r}
library(fpp2)

TOTALNSA <- read.csv("TOTALNSA.csv")
TOTALNSA_ts <- ts(TOTALNSA$TOTALNSA, start = c(1976, 1), frequency = 12)

# 1. Examine the data
# This plot shows vehicle sales over time and helps identify seasonal patterns.
head(TOTALNSA_ts)
plot(TOTALNSA_ts)
```
```{r}
stl_decomp <- stl(TOTALNSA_ts, s.window = "periodic")
plot(stl_decomp)
attributes(stl_decomp)
# STL separates vehicle sales into seasonal, trend, and remainder components.
```
```{r}
seasadj(stl_decomp)

plot(TOTALNSA_ts)
lines(seasadj(stl_decomp), col = "red")
# Seasonal adjustment removes recurring seasonal effects to make the underlying sales pattern easier to examine.
```
```{r}
f_stl <- forecast(stl_decomp, h = 15)
f_stl
plot(f_stl)
# This model forecasts vehicle sales for the next 15 months using the trend and seasonal patterns.
```
```{r}
decomp_add <- decompose(TOTALNSA_ts, type = "additive")
attributes(decomp_add)
plot(decomp_add)
seasadj(decomp_add)
# The additive model assumes seasonal changes stay approximately constant in size over time.
```
```{r}
decomp_mult <- decompose(TOTALNSA_ts, type = "multiplicative")
attributes(decomp_mult)
plot(decomp_mult)
seasadj(decomp_mult)
# The multiplicative model assumes seasonal changes vary proportionally with the overall sales level.
```
```{r}
log_TOTALNSA <- log(TOTALNSA_ts)

stl_log <- stl(log_TOTALNSA, s.window = "periodic")
plot(stl_log)

seasadj_mult <- exp(seasadj(stl_log))
head(seasadj_mult)
# Taking the logarithm allows STL to examine proportional seasonal patterns; the adjusted values are then converted back to the original scale.
```
